title: Streaming tool-call serialization causing gradual memory growth + Hosted 5xx during customer escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customer escalations started on 2026-03-01 after several customers enabling function-calling and streaming responses observed intermittent 5xx errors and abrupt session terminations. Symptoms were concentrated on Hosted multitenant nodes handling long-running streaming sessions where individual tool integrations returned large JSON payloads (100KB-1MB) per tool call.

What happened (triage notes):
- Multiple customers reported repeated 5xx and truncated streams during function/tool calling.
- Runtime alerting showed an increase in OOM kills and worker restarts on a subset of serving pools (us-west-2-hosted-pool-3).
- Heap profiles captured during incidents show monotonic memory growth correlated with the streaming serialization path: the runtime was buffering whole tool responses to serialize them into the streaming protocol frame instead of streaming them incrementally.
- The issue manifested under a combination of: large tool response sizes, simultaneous multiplexed streaming sessions, and the legacy JSON stringify path that materializes the entire tool result in memory before framing.

Root cause (analysis):
- The streaming handler used a convenience path that collected tool outputs into an in-memory array and invoked JSON.stringify() to produce the final frame. For small tool outputs this was fine; for larger outputs across many concurrent sessions this led to per-worker memory amplification and eventual OOMs, returning 5xx to tenants on that worker.
- The regression surfaced after a function-calling performance refactor (runtime commit: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime@b7f3a2) that introduced an eager-serialization helper to normalize tool objects for schema validation. The helper didn't account for streaming/large-payload codepaths.

Immediate mitigations applied (what we did):
- Rolled out a quick server-side guard that rejects tool response objects > 256KB with a 422 and human-friendly guidance to the customer (temporary stop-gap) to prevent OOM cascades. Deployed at 2026-03-02 14:30 UTC to hosted pools.
- Added an emergency per-worker streaming memory cap and early backpressure signal to the admission path to prevent new long-running streams from landing on a worker with high memorystate.
- Hotfix PR created to switch the serialization path to incremental streaming (stream JSON tokenization into frames) and to avoid retaining full objects in memory: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1489. Patch landed on a feature branch; currently under integration tests.
- Customer comms: PM drafted a status update and targeted messages to impacted customers with remediation suggestions (use smaller tool outputs or enable dedicated capacity).

Planned permanent fix / rollout plan:
1) Merge PR 1489 after e2e and stress tests (goal: 2026-03-13). Tests will run sustained-concurrency streaming workloads with tool payload sizes up to 1MB to validate memory usage.
2) Canary rollout to 5% of hosted streaming traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 24h with aggressive OOM / latency alerts.
3) Progressive ramp to 50% then 100% with rollback gates tied to p95 latency and OOM rate.
4) Add unit+integration tests that assert streaming serialization does not allocate >20% more heap vs baseline across payload sizes to catch regressions.
5) SDK guidance: publish a best-practices note and add an SDK header to indicate "streaming-structured-tool" usage so client tooling can opt-in to chunked responses.

Monitoring & observability changes (short-term + long-term):
- Short-term: added a new metric runtime.stream_writer.buffer_bytes and an alert on sustained per-worker buffer_bytes > 64MB sustained for 30s.
- Long-term: add a tracing span for tool-serialization with sampled heap profiles attached to traces that exceed memory thresholds.

Customer impact and communication:
- Impact: high for a small subset of customers using streaming + function-calling with large tool responses. Several customers experienced production errors and opened escalations with support.
- Communication: PMs have scheduled a targeted RCA follow-up with impacted customers for 2026-03-15. We’ve provided short-term workarounds and eligibility for free Dedicated trial for customers with regulatory needs who cannot adapt payload size quickly.

Follow-ups / postmortem actions (owner assignments):
- Jordan Meyers (assignee): own PR validation, canary rollout, and rollback automation (ENG-110555).
- Priya Rao (runtime): implement and own incremental JSON tokenizer tests (follow-up ticket: ENG-110556).
- Support (Lina Ortega): compile escalations timeline, affected customer list, and coordinate postmortem invites.
- Docs (DevRel): update SDK docs with chunking guidance and example helpers.

Notes & artifacts:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1489
- Stress-run artifacts (internal GCS): gs://redwood-qa/streaming-oom/2026-03-03/
- Customer escalation thread (Zendesk): ZD#48291
- Initial heap flame graphs (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1exampleheapgraphs

Expected completion: target full rollout by 2026-03-18 if canary remains healthy.

2026-03-04 - Priya Rao: Added tokenizer unit tests. Noted one edge-case with circular refs in tool objects - added safe stringify fallback for that case.
2026-03-05 - Lina Ortega (Support): Sent customer comms with workaround and offered Dedicated trial for two enterprise customers still blocked.
